---
title: "Evolutionary invasion analysis"
subtitle: "Otto & Day, chapter 12, with PracticalCAS"
engine: julia
---

To ask which trait evolves, let the resident reach its equilibrium and ask
whether a rare mutant can grow: its invasion fitness `W(m, r)`. Singular
strategies, where the selection gradient `∂W/∂m` at `m = r` vanishes, are
classified by second derivatives into evolutionary end points (CSS),
branching points, Garden-of-Eden points and repellers.

```{julia}
using PracticalCAS
```

## The evolution of virulence

A pathogen strain with virulence `α` (extra host death rate) transmits at
rate `β(α) = b√α`, so more virulent strains transmit more but with
diminishing returns; hosts die at rate `μ` and recover at rate `γ`. With the resident
strain at equilibrium, susceptibles sit at `S* = (μ + α_r + γ)/β(α_r)`, and a
rare mutant strain's infected hosts change at the per-capita rate

```{julia}
@syms S::nonneg I::nonneg Iₘ::nonneg m::positive r::positive μ::positive γ::positive b::positive θ::positive Λ::positive
β(x) = b * sqrt(x)                     # a transmission–virulence trade-off
model = ode(S => Λ - β(r) * S * I - β(m) * S * Iₘ - μ * S,
            I => β(r) * S * I - (μ + r + γ) * I,
            Iₘ => β(m) * S * Iₘ - (μ + m + γ) * Iₘ)
endemic = only(e for e in equilibria(ode(S => Λ - β(r) * S * I - μ * S, I => β(r) * S * I - (μ + r + γ) * I)) if !iszero(e[I]))
W = invasion_fitness(model.rhs[3], Iₘ, endemic)
```

The mutant invades when it has a higher `R₀ = β(α)/(μ + α + γ)`, so
evolution maximises `R₀`. The singular strategy is an evolutionary end point:

```{julia}
cs = classify_singular(W, m, r)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(W, β(m) * (μ + r + γ) / β(r) - (μ + m + γ))
c = only(c for c in cs if decide(c.value > 0) !== false)
@assert c.kind === :CSS
@assert isequiv(c.value, μ + γ)

R0(x) = β(x) / (μ + x + γ)
@assert isequiv(simplify(subs(diff(R0(m), m), m => c.value)), 0)
```

## Branching: competition for a continuum of resources

With carrying capacity `K(x) = K₀ exp(-x²/(2σ²))` peaking at trait 0 and
competition between traits `m`, `r` falling off as `exp(-(m - r)²/(2τ²))`,
the invasion fitness is

```{julia}
@syms σ::positive τ::positive
K(z) = exp(-z^2 / (2σ^2))
Wc = 1 - exp(-(m - r)^2 / (2τ^2)) * K(r) / K(m)
sc = only(classify_singular(Wc, m, r))
```

Trait 0 is always convergence stable, but it is evolutionarily stable only if
competition is broader than the resource distribution; otherwise the
population branches into two:

```{julia}
assuming(τ < σ) do
    only(classify_singular(Wc, m, r)).kind
end
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert iszero(sc.value)
@assert decide(sc.convergence) === true
@assert assuming(() -> only(classify_singular(Wc, m, r)).kind, τ < σ) === :branching
@assert assuming(() -> only(classify_singular(Wc, m, r)).kind, τ > σ) === :CSS
```

## A game: hawks and doves

When fitness depends on what others do, the ESS of a matrix game can be found
directly (see also the replicator dynamics):

```{julia}
@syms V::positive C::positive
ess(hawk_dove(V, C))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
mixed = only(e for e in ess(hawk_dove(V, C)) if length(e.support) == 2)
@assert isequiv(mixed.x[1], V / C)
```

## Invasion with class structure

A mutant with juvenile survival `sₘ` in a population of residents with
survival `s_r`: juveniles `Jₘ` mature to adults `Aₘ`, which produce juveniles
at a rate reduced by density, `f/(1 + N)`. The invasion matrix is the
linearisation of the mutant classes at the resident equilibrium.

```{julia}
@syms J::nonneg Aᵣ::nonneg Jₘ::nonneg Aₘ::nonneg sᵣ::(0, 1) sₘ::(0, 1) f::positive a::(0, 1)
N = Aᵣ + Aₘ
st = recurrence(J => f * Aᵣ / (1 + N), Aᵣ => sᵣ * J + a * Aᵣ,
                Jₘ => f * Aₘ / (1 + N), Aₘ => sₘ * Jₘ + a * Aₘ)
res = recurrence(J => f * Aᵣ / (1 + Aᵣ), Aᵣ => sᵣ * J + a * Aᵣ)
eqr = only(e for e in equilibria(res) if !iszero(e[Aᵣ]))
invd = invasion_fitness(st, [Jₘ, Aₘ], eqr)
invd.matrix
```

At `sₘ = sᵣ` the resident equilibrium has growth factor 1; the selection
gradient, from the reproductive values and stable distribution of the
invasion matrix, is positive: higher juvenile survival is favoured.

```{julia}
Am = invd.matrix

grad = selection_gradient(subs(Am, sₘ => m, sᵣ => r), m, r)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert ispositive(grad) || decide(grad > 0) === true
# the same from the eigenvalue: λ(sₘ) solves det(Am - λI) = 0 with λ = 1 at sₘ = sᵣ
@syms λ
cp = charpoly(subs(Am, sₘ => m, sᵣ => r), λ)
dλ = simplify(subs(-diff(cp, m) / diff(cp, λ), λ => 1, m => r))
@assert isequiv(grad, dλ)
```
